# ECN-2026-042 Change notice - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Reason for change
- Background: During routine maintenance and operational review, engineering identified a need to formalize and communicate the maximum allowable system pressure limit for the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03). The intent is to reduce risk of hydraulic component stress that could lead to premature wear or failure, and to align lockout tagout, maintenance, and SOP references with operational controls. This change also corrects variance between operator practice and equipment documentation found during a recent internal audit.
- Rationale: Establishing a clear, documented system pressure limit will standardize commissioning checks, test procedures, and emergency response. It minimizes ambiguity for operations and maintenance personnel, ensures compatibility with hydraulic accessories, and supports compliance with machine safety reviews. The specified limit is applicable to all hydraulic circuits that are part of the press system and its ancillary equipment as defined in related documents.

Affected items
- Primary equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03 is subject to this change. All onboard hydraulic circuits, pressure sensors, relief valves, and pressure-limiting devices that govern system pressure are affected.
- Documentation: The following documents shall be updated to reflect the change and to provide consistent instructions across operations and maintenance: ECN-2026-049, MM-P2-L4-HP03, SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Procedures and training: Operator checklists, daily start procedures, and maintenance task plans that reference allowable pressure ranges must be revised. Training materials used for new and reassigned operators and maintenance personnel require update to include the new system pressure limit and associated verification steps.
- Spare parts and calibration: Any pressure transducers, gauges, or relief valves that are selected or staged for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 must be compatible with the established limit. Calibration records for pressure-sensing devices will reflect verification against the updated acceptance criteria.

Implementation
- New limit: The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar. This value is the maximum allowable system pressure for all applicable hydraulic circuits on the press.
- Engineering actions: Engineering will issue updated schematics and stamped notes that identify the locations where the system pressure limit applies. Relief valve setpoint documentation will be adjusted to ensure that settings and redundancy meet the new limit.
- Controls modification: PLC setpoints and alarm thresholds that reference system pressure shall be adjusted to trigger warnings below the limit and to initiate safe shutdown logic if pressure approaches the limit. All changes to control logic will be reviewed and tested in a controlled environment and recorded in the change log.
- Maintenance instructions: Maintenance work plans will include a mandatory verification step that confirms system pressure does not exceed the specified limit before any pressure-bearing fasteners are released or any hydraulic lines are opened. These verifications shall be recorded on maintenance service reports and stored with the asset history for EQ-P2-L4-HP03.
- Commissioning and acceptance: After implementation, a controlled pressure test will be performed to demonstrate compliance. Test execution will be recorded, including the instrumentation used and calibration certificates for pressure measurement devices. The acceptance record will be retained with maintenance files and referenced in MM-P2-L4-HP03.
- Operator procedures: Operator tasks and start sequences will incorporate a pressure check to verify that system pressure remains below the specified limit prior to cyclic loading. Any excursion must be logged and escalated per SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Examples of application: When replacing a hydraulic hose assembly on EQ-P2-L4-HP03, maintenance personnel shall confirm system pressure is verified below the limit before depressurizing the line. When performing a pressure sensor replacement, technicians will validate the new sensor against calibrated equipment and document that readings correlate and remain below the limit during functional testing.

Records to keep
- Record types: Change implementation checklist, updated schematics, control logic revision log, pressure test reports, instrument calibration certificates, maintenance service reports, operator training acknowledgement records, and audit evidence of procedural updates.
- Storage location: Records will be filed in the document control system under the equipment folder for EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and cross-referenced in the ECN record. Related document updates will reference ECN-2026-049, MM-P2-L4-HP03, and SOP-P2-L4-03.
- Retention note: All records associated with this change shall be retained as part of the asset history and made available for inspection during internal and external audits.

Approvals
- Approval requirements: The following approvals are required prior to implementation: engineering review and signoff, maintenance management approval, operations supervision acceptance, and document control closure. Each approver shall verify that procedures, control logic changes, and training materials have been updated and that records are in place.
- Post-implementation review: After initial implementation, a focused operational review will verify that the system pressure limit is being observed in day-to-day use and that alarms and interlocks function as intended. Findings will be documented and any corrective actions will follow the standard change management path referencing ECN-2026-049.
- Related documentation: Use this ECN in conjunction with ECN-2026-049, and ensure consistency with the maintenance manual MM-P2-L4-HP03 and the standard operating procedure SOP-P2-L4-03 for operational and maintenance guidance.

Prepared by: Engineering  
Distribution: Operations, Maintenance, Document Control, Safety

Attachments: Implementation checklist, updated schematic extract, sample pressure test report template, training slide excerpt.
